external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and puts jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker process that picks up jobs and does the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue receiving jobs from the web application for the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The web application's configuration store, holding the credentials it needs for the queue.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The worker's configuration store, holding the credentials it needs for the database.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to application
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks them up
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config
data_flows.data_description: web application settings and queue credentials

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: over HTTP/S across the public internet

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier behind the web tier containing the queue, worker and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because the user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source says that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker is internal because it is in the backend tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source places the worker in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than an application-facing web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a background worker process that picks up jobs and does the work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web application config holds the credentials the process needs.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source says the worker config holds the credentials the process needs.
